Cost-based query optimizer (CBO) translating logical plans using column statistics histograms
Vectorized execution engine processing blocks of tuples to minimize virtual dispatch overhead
Lock-free page cache implementing an eviction policy with atomic handle tracking

candidate_ideas.name: NexusQL Engine
candidate_ideas.pain: Standard database internals are buried behind massive legacy codebases, making it difficult to study or experiment with custom cost-based optimizers and lock-free execution engines.
candidate_ideas.problem: Single-node relational databases often bottleneck on locking contention and lack a custom-built, cost-based query optimizer and vectorized execution pipeline built entirely from scratch.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency relational database storage and execution engine written in Java 21 featuring a custom SQL parser, a cost-based optimizer using catalog histograms, a lock-free page cache, and a vectorized Volcano-style iterator model.
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic integration suite executing malformed SQL statements, synthetic out-of-order transaction histories, concurrent write stress tests, and corrupted binary page recovery verification.

major_features: Custom lexer and recursive-descent parser supporting statements, functions, and closures
Stack-based bytecode compiler translating AST nodes into dense numeric opcodes
Virtual machine execution loop managing explicit call frames, stack pointers, and registers
Reference-counting memory manager tracking heap allocations with metadata headers
Cycle-detection garbage collection pass resolving deferred circular reference graphs
First-class closure implementation capturing and retaining outer lexical environment scopes
Built-in foreign function interface (FFI) bindings for executing host system routines
Disassembler subsystem formatting binary bytecode streams into human-readable assembly
candidate_ideas.name: Kerno Runtime
candidate_ideas.pain: Writing a complete language runtime from scratch requires handling complex edge cases like reference cycle breaking, stack frame unwinding, and precise symbol table resolution.
candidate_ideas.problem: Higher-level languages abstract away memory management and stack layout, hiding how closures, lexical scoping, and automatic reference counting function at the machine level.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency lexical-scoping interpreter and reference-counting virtual machine implemented in C11, featuring a custom AST compiler, first-class closures, dynamic environment frames, and a cycle-detecting reference tracker.
candidate_ideas.verification: Test suite featuring invalid syntax trees, recursive reference cycles, uninitialized variable access, stack overflow boundary conditions, and memory leak verification scripts.

major_features: Custom binary wire protocol supporting framed message payloads and multiplexed streams
Segmented append-only on-disk log storage with configurable byte-size and time rotation
Consumer group coordination engine handling dynamic partition assignment and heartbeats
Explicit message acknowledgment (ACK) and offset commit tracking loops
Non-blocking TCP network server utilizing Java 21 Selector and SocketChannel multiplexing
Zero-copy file transfer pipeline utilizing NIO FileChannel and socket transmission
Configurable retention policy enforcing background disk compaction and segment pruning
Deterministic integration harness simulating network packet drops and socket delays
candidate_ideas.name: SentryStream
candidate_ideas.pain: Building a fault-tolerant message queue requires manual handling of segment file rotation, offset tracking, and asynchronous network selector multiplexing without external dependencies.
candidate_ideas.problem: Enterprise message brokers are heavily bloated, while lightweight socket servers lack robust consumer group coordination, message deduplication, and zero-copy log persistence.
candidate_ideas.solution: A high-performance append-only message log and broker written in Java 21, implementing a custom binary wire protocol, zero-copy file segment mapping, consumer group offset rebalancing, and retention compaction.
candidate_ideas.verification: Test harness injecting socket connection drops, corrupt length-prefixed frames, overlapping consumer group rebalances, and disk-full write exceptions.

major_features: Self-balancing B+Tree node splitting and merging algorithms implemented on binary blocks
Fixed-size node layout supporting key-value slot compaction and pointer management
On-disk binary serialization layout with embedded CRC32 integrity verification checksums
Range query iterator supporting forward and backward traversal across disk leaf nodes
Write-Ahead Log (WAL) recording structural mutations for crash recovery
LRU block cache managing memory-mapped file pages with pin-count locking
Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) maintaining historical node versions for snapshots
Background compaction utility defragmenting split leaf nodes and reclaiming free pages
candidate_ideas.name: ApexIndex
candidate_ideas.pain: Writing a self-balancing B+Tree or LSM-tree index from scratch requires complex node splitting, page layout serialization, and concurrency control logic.
candidate_ideas.problem: Standard disk-based storage struggles to maintain sub-millisecond range queries over high-cardinality keys without consuming excessive RAM or suffering from fragmentation.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency disk-backed B+Tree indexing engine written in Python 3.12, providing node splitting, batched transactional updates, MVCC iteration, and binary block serialization with CRC32 verification.
candidate_ideas.verification: Comprehensive test suite covering root node splits under high-volume insertions, missing key lookups, malformed disk blocks, and concurrent read-write transaction isolation.

major_features: Deterministic state-transition planner evaluating rule graphs via forward chaining
Working memory subsystem maintaining typed facts with automated TTL expiration
Constraint validation engine detecting and resolving contradictory belief states
Heuristic scoring module ranking prospective action paths based on local weights
Immutable audit log recording every inference step and state mutation with timestamps
Bounded context window manager dropping stale facts according to priority policies
Explicit feedback adaptation loop adjusting internal weight parameters from local telemetry
Virtual Thread-based concurrent rule evaluation engine processing decoupled sub-goals
candidate_ideas.name: CognitiveGrid Agent
candidate_ideas.pain: Designing an autonomous local agent without heavy external frameworks requires managing explicit belief-desire-intent loops, rule constraints, and bounded memory buffers manually.
candidate_ideas.problem: Local decision-making agents often lack a transparent, inspectable constraint engine and deterministic state-transition memory, relying on opaque probabilistic black boxes.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency local reasoning agent engine written in Java 21, implementing a deterministic state-transition planner, a working memory rule engine, local heuristic scoring, and immutable audit logs.
candidate_ideas.verification: Test framework evaluating conflicting constraint rules, cyclic goal dependencies, bounded memory overflow conditions, and corrupted state restoration sequences.

known_limitations: Gemini discovery reasons from model knowledge; the factory does not claim live market research or verified market demand.

A passing systems release proves the generated source compiled or byte-compiled and its factory-required unit/integration suites passed; it does not by itself prove production-scale reliability, security certification, or benchmark superiority.
Generated systems projects intentionally use standard-library-only Java 21, C11, or Python 3.12 profiles so validation can be deterministic and does not depend on unverifiable third-party packages.

Hard projects are scoped implementations of real mechanisms, not claims of complete compatibility with Redis, full SQL standards, industrial compilers, or frontier machine-learning systems unless the tests and documentation explicitly demonstrate that scope.
